title: 1995 AMC 8 Problem 18
statement: The area of each of the four congruent L-shaped regions of this \(100\)-inch by \(100\)-inch square is \(\dfrac{3}{16}\) of the total area. How many inches long is the side of the center square?

solutions.text:
The four L-shaped regions cover \(4 \times \dfrac{3}{16} = \dfrac34\) of the square, so the center square is the remaining \(\dfrac14\) of the total area.

The total area is \(100 \times 100 = 10000\) square inches, so the center square has area \(\dfrac14 \times 10000 = 2500,\) and its side is \(\sqrt{2500} = 50\) inches.

Thus, the correct answer is C .
hints: The four L-shaped regions together make up \(4 \times \dfrac{3}{16}\) of the square
The center square is the remaining fraction of the area; its side is the square root of its area
